facts.label: Source register
facts.text: Version relationships. The three 10-Qs are separate periodic reports for successive periods, not versions of each other; none supersedes the 10-K. Each release is a separate source for its quarter and is retained beside the filing for the same quarter. The 10-K and the 10-Qs share one registrant, so there is no parent, subsidiary or combined-filing split to resolve. Within the debt, the 10-Q Q3 names the roles it prints: the Company as issuer of the Secured Notes; guarantors are "each domestic and Canadian subsidiary of the Company that is a borrower under, or a guarantor of" the ABL Credit Facility (10-Q Q3 page:18); euro notes were issued by the Company's "wholly owned subsidiary" (10-Q Q3 page:18), named on page:28 as Whirlpool Finance Luxembourg S.a.r.l.; the 10-K states that "For outstanding notes issued by our wholly-owned subsidiaries the debt is fully and unconditionally guaranteed by the Company" (10-K page:101). No restricted or unrestricted subsidiary distinction is printed.

facts.label: Strongest contrary evidence and what the sources do not settle
facts.text: - Perimeter. The 10-K says that "the operations previously reported within the MDA Asia segment are no longer reported as a segment as a result of the deconsolidation of Whirlpool India" (10-K page:4), and the Q3 release flags the 2025 comparative as including the India business (release Q3 page:1). A trend analysis that does not adjust for this would overstate the decline; the release itself shows a like-for-like organic sales measure that removes India sales (release Q3 page:26). The sources do not print a full like-for-like FY2025 income statement. - Definition difference. Segment-note total EBIT for Q3 2026 is "$ (128)" (10-Q Q3 page:43) and ties to the release's reported EBIT of "$ (128)"; the release's ongoing EBIT of "$ 97" (release Q3 page:11) excludes restructuring, an equity method impairment, M&A costs and a trade customer bankruptcy charge. The two are different measures, both issuer-defined, and downstream modules must label which they use. - Management claim versus filing. The release says the company has "preserved a clear debt maturity ladder until 2028" (release Q3 page:1). The 10-Q Q3 supports part of this: "We have $14 million of debt maturing in the next twelve months" (10-Q Q3 page:53). The 10-Q does not itself print a maturity table after the refinancing, so the 2028 claim is an attributed management statement that a downstream module cannot verify from a table. - Net leverage. The releases define "Net debt leverage" and "Ongoing EBITDA" (release Q3 page:9) but the pinned text does not print a computed ratio. The release outlook gives "Net debt below $4.5 billion at year end" (release Q3 page:2), a forward management statement, not a reported ratio.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: Whirlpool entered the latest quarter with weaker earnings and a much longer, more secured debt stack than a year earlier. On the company's own ongoing EBIT plus cash flow depreciation and amortization, EBITDA for the twelve months to September 30, 2026 is 720 million, down from 1,067 million in FY2025 and 1,220 million in FY2024. Total debt (notes payable, current maturities and long-term debt) was 6,852 million at September 30, 2026 against 6,520 million at December 31, 2025, so total debt over ongoing EBITDA is 9.52x against 6.11x, and net debt over ongoing EBITDA is 7.98x against 5.48x. Using the reported operating profit basis instead, the same ratios are 8.46x and 7.10x for the latest twelve months, and the direction is the same. Reported earnings were also hit in the third quarter by a 124 million impairment of the Whirlpool India equity stake and a 54 million trade customer bankruptcy charge, and flattered in earlier periods by disposal gains. The June 2026 refinancing, funded with 2,000 million of second lien notes and a 2,000 million asset-based facility that was undrawn at quarter end, removed the 2026 and 2027 euro note maturities; the sources do not print a post-refinancing maturity table, so the maturity chart below is derived. Cash from operations was negative 826 million for nine months 2026, and management's own guidance for year-end net debt requires a very large fourth-quarter working capital inflow. These conclusions are about the financial base only; interim cash interest, borrowing base availability and covenant definitions are not supplied, and every ratio here depends on the stated EBITDA definition.

It excludes lease liabilities (noncurrent 863 at 2026-09-30, 10-Q Q3 page:6), pensions and retiree medical (83 and 91 on the same page), the 575 mandatory convertible preferred, supply chain finance of 650 recorded in accounts payable (10-Q Q3 page:12) and 157 of transferred receivables still serviced by the Company (10-Q Q3 page:23). - EBITDA is not a printed figure. facts.text: - Leverage. Total debt rose by 332 from December 31, 2025 to September 30, 2026 (6,520 to 6,852) while ongoing EBITDA fell, so the ratio worsened on both terms. Ongoing EBITDA over interest expense fell from 3.13x in FY2025 to 2.21x over the latest twelve months. The Q3 2026 interest expense of 102 is the highest quarter in the series shown and comes after the June issue of the 7.500% and 7.875% secured notes and the repayment of the euro notes and bank debt; the sources do not print the run-rate effect or attribute the increase. The 10-K facility required interest coverage of at least 3.0 (10-K page:104), and a May 2026 amendment excluded the March 31, 2026 quarter from that test (10-Q Q1 page:17). The new ABL has a springing fixed charge coverage ratio of not less than 1.00 to 1.00, tested only if Availability falls below the greater of 10% of the Line Cap and 135 (10-Q Q3 pages:20-21); the level and headroom cannot be computed from the sources. - Cash flow quality. Cash used in operations was 826 for nine months 2026 against 669 used in nine months 2025, with accounts payable (306), accrued advertising and promotions (318) and other (168) among the larger movements (10-Q Q3 page:7). Management guides full-year cash from operations of about 700 and free cash flow of about 300 (Release Q3 page:2), which implies a fourth-quarter operating inflow of about 1,526 (700 less the nine-month outflow of 826 as a negative); this is derived from guidance, not reported. - Liquidity. Cash of 1,103 and 2,193 of undrawn committed facilities total 3,296, down from 4,101 at December 31, 2025 (669 plus 3,432). The nominal undrawn amount overstates usable liquidity because the ABL is limited by a borrowing base and by the springing covenant, and because letters of credit that may use the ABL are not printed. rows.label: Leverage on company ongoing earnings plus depreciation rose to 9.52x total debt for the twelve months to Q3 2026 from 6.11x in FY2025, with debt of 6,852 million. The June refinancing cleared 2026 and 2027 maturities.
Ongoing EBITDA for the latest twelve months is 720 million against 1,067 million in FY2025, while total debt moved little.
The June 2026 refinancing replaced unsecured bank debt and the 2026 and 2027 euro notes with second lien notes and a secured asset-based facility.
Nine-month cash from operations was negative 826 million, and year-end net debt guidance relies on a large fourth-quarter inflow.
Cash was 1,103 million and undrawn committed facilities were 2,193 million at September 30, 2026.
Cash paid for interest is printed only for full years.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Whirlpool is a listed, widely held major and small appliance manufacturer with no sponsor named in the sources, and its recent transactions have been defensive: sell down non-core stakes, raise equity, cut distributions, and refinance bank and euro debt into secured paper. The business is concentrated in North America, which supplied most nine-month 2026 net sales of 10,467 million through MDA North America at 7,141 million, and in one retail channel, with Lowe's about 15% of 2025 net sales. Demand in North America is soft, tariffs and cost inflation are compressing margins, and management has cut its 2026 earnings outlook twice since May. The June 2026 refinancing gave the company a 2,000 million asset-based facility, undrawn at quarter end, and replaced the 2026 and 2027 euro notes with second lien notes, so near-term maturities are cleared at the cost of subordinating unsecured creditors in the collateral pool. Governance behaviour in the sources is on balance supportive of liquidity (equity issuance, dividend cuts, asset sales and sale-leasebacks) with a mixed effect on creditor ranking. The decisive unknowns are legal: what the indentures permit, what the ABL borrowing base allows, and who the large holders are, none of which is supplied. Source evidence is primary and dated, except management characterisations, which are labelled.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The transactions that matter to creditors are these, all dated on or before the cutoff of 2026-11-05. On February 27, 2026 Whirlpool issued 11,500,000 depositary shares of its 8.50% Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock (net cash proceeds 557 million) and 7,898,550 common shares at 69 dollars per share (net cash proceeds 524 million), and used about 900 million of the proceeds to repay part of its prior revolving credit facility (10-Q Q3 pages:52-53, 57). In March 2026 it paid 157 million to buy the legal title to five assets previously held under synthetic leases (10-Q Q3 page:11). In May 2026 it amended the Long-Term Credit Agreement to cut the commitment from 3.50 billion to 2.25 billion, excluded the March 31, 2026 quarter from the interest coverage test and required a full refinancing before July 1, 2026 (10-Q Q1 page:17). In June 2026 it agreed with Arcelik to sell its remaining 25% of Beko Europe, terminate deferred rights from the 2022 Russian business divestiture and release accrued indemnities, for net cash of 84 million plus a 2.9% Arcelik stake, booking a gain of 139 million (10-Q Q3 pages:13, 46). On June 16, 2026 it issued 1,000 million of 7.500% Senior Secured Second Lien Notes due 2031 and 1,000 million of 7.875% Senior Secured Second Lien Notes due 2034 under a Rule 144A private placement, entered a new asset-based credit facility of up to 2,000 million with J.P. Morgan as agent, and terminated the Long-Term Credit Agreement; the notes and the facility share one collateral pool, first-priority for the facility and second-priority for the notes, guaranteed by domestic and Canadian subsidiaries that are ABL obligors. The proceeds and ABL borrowings repaid the 1.250% Senior Notes due 2026, the 1.100% Senior Notes due 2027 and the unsecured revolver by July 1, 2026, with 212 million of cash restricted at June 30 for that payment (10-Q Q3 pages:17-21; 10-Q Q2 page:7). The indenture limits additional debt, restricted payments, liens, investments, asset sales and mergers, requires a 101% change of control offer and may require asset-sale offers at 100% (10-Q Q3 page:18). The ABL carries a springing fixed charge coverage test of 1.00 to 1.00 when Availability falls below the greater of 10% of the Line Cap and 135 (10-Q Q3 pages:20-21). Other liquidity actions were sale-leasebacks of two assets for about 111 million in June and one for about 59 million in September, with initial annual rent of about 9 million and 5 million, and a receivables purchase agreement amended in Q3 to capacity of up to 250 million with a first-priority security interest for the purchaser in unsold program receivables (10-Q Q3 pages:11-12, 23). On July 1, 2026 it announced the Supsa plant closure. In Q3 2026 it recorded a 124 million impairment of its Whirlpool India stake and a 54 million charge on the Casas Bahia bankruptcy reorganization (10-Q Q3 pages:14, 55). The December 2025 background is the sale of about 11% of Whirlpool India for about 166 million, reducing ownership from 51% to about 40%, with deconsolidation and a gain of 251 million (10-Q Q3 page:45). Debt raised in 2026 and its effect on the debt stack and liquidity are quantified in CP-1: total debt of 6,852 million, cash of 1,103 million and undrawn committed facilities of 2,193 million at September 30, 2026. No transaction was reported after September 30, 2026 other than management statements in the October 26, 2026 release (Q4 price increases and the net debt expectation); the 10-Q Q3 reports "ITEM 5. OTHER INFORMATION None." (10-Q Q3 page:68). The executed indenture and ABL agreement are not supplied, so lien, guarantee, baskets and permitted payment terms are known only as the issuer summarises them.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Whirlpool is a stretched, non-investment-grade credit with a funded runway to 2028 but little earnings cushion. The strongest support is liquidity and structure: USD 1,103 million of cash and USD 2,193 million of undrawn committed facilities at September 30, 2026, equity raised in February, and only USD 14 million due within twelve months after the June refinancing. The weakest point is earnings: ongoing EBITDA for the latest twelve months is USD 720 million against total debt of USD 6,852 million, or 9.52x, with operating cash flow of negative USD 826 million for nine months and interest expense now running near USD 100 million a quarter. What decides the outcome is whether price increases and cost take-out restore North American margins, and whether year-end working capital release materialises, before the secured facility's borrowing base and its fixed charge test begin to bind.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Leverage has moved sharply the wrong way. Total debt over ongoing EBITDA was 5.43x in FY2024, 6.11x in FY2025 and is 9.52x for the twelve months to September 30, 2026, with net debt over ongoing EBITDA of 7.98x. On the stricter operating-profit basis the latest ratios are 8.46x and 7.10x, so the conclusion does not depend on which EBITDA is used. Total debt rose by USD 332 million over the first nine months of 2026 while ongoing EBITDA fell from USD 1,067 million in FY2025 to USD 720 million for the latest twelve months. The issuer does not print a leverage ratio, so every ratio here is analyst-built.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The refinancing bought time and cost carry. The June 2026 issue of USD 1,000 million of 7.500% notes due 2031 and USD 1,000 million of 7.875% notes due 2034 carries about USD 154 million of annual coupon (derived from the stated rates), replacing euro notes with coupons of 1.25% and 1.10% on about USD 1,290 million of carrying value, so roughly USD 139 million of added annual coupon before any saving on the repaid revolver. Quarterly interest expense reached USD 102 million in Q3 2026 against USD 63 million in Q2, and management guides full-year 2026 interest of about USD 350 million and Q4 interest of about USD 103 million. Ongoing EBITDA over annualised Q3 interest of USD 408 million is 1.76x, and guided full-year 2026 ongoing EBIT of about USD 293 million is 0.84x guided interest. Cash interest is not printed for the interim periods, so these are expense-based.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liquidity is adequate on paper and uncertain in substance. Cash of USD 1,103 million and undrawn commitments of USD 2,193 million total USD 3,296 million, down from USD 4,101 million at December 31, 2025, and the nominal undrawn amount is mostly an ABL (USD 2,000 million) limited by a borrowing base the filings do not disclose. Operating cash flow was negative USD 826 million for nine months and management's guidance of about USD 700 million for the year implies a fourth-quarter inflow of about USD 1,526 million. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Covenant headroom is thin on every proxy available. The ABL tests fixed charge coverage of 1.00x only when Availability falls below the greater of 10% of the Line Cap and USD 135 million. An indicative proxy of ongoing EBITDA less capital expenditures over interest expense is 0.97x, so if availability tightened the test could bind. The proxy is not the covenant definition. The prior facility's interest coverage test of at least 3.0x was relaxed in May 2026 by excluding the first quarter, and expense-based cover has since fallen to 2.21x.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Whirlpool holds scaled, long-established appliance franchises with leading positions in the Americas and a brand portfolio including Whirlpool, KitchenAid and Maytag (Documentary Fact; Management Language for the market-position wording). It has demonstrated market access in 2026, raising USD 524 million of common equity and USD 557 million of mandatory convertible preferred in February (Documentary Fact), and it suspended the common dividend, which retains cash (Documentary Fact). After the June refinancing near-term maturities are cleared: USD 14 million falls due in the next twelve months and USD 585 million in 2028 (Documentary Fact for the 14; Analyst Interpretation for the schedule, which is rebuilt). The asset-based facility of USD 2,000 million and Brazilian facilities of USD 193 million were undrawn at September 30, 2026 (Documentary Fact). Management is executing structural cost take-out and price increases, announced at 7% in North America and up to 10% in Latin America (Management Language), and the SDA Global segment earned segment EBIT of USD 124 million on USD 710 million of nine-month sales (Documentary Fact).

facts.text: Weaknesses. Leverage of 9.52x total debt over ongoing EBITDA is high and rising (Analyst Interpretation on a Documentary Fact base). Ongoing EBIT for Q3 2026 was USD 97 million against USD 180 million a year earlier and management has cut its 2026 earnings outlook twice since May (Documentary Fact; Management Language for the outlook). North American demand is soft and one retailer is about 15% of sales and about 44% of receivables (Documentary Fact). Operating cash flow is negative on a nine-month basis, and year-end net debt guidance relies on a fourth-quarter release (Analyst Interpretation). The new secured structure subordinates unsecured creditors in the collateral pool and limits flexibility through indenture covenants and a borrowing base (Documentary Fact; legal capacity Insufficient Information). Ratings are below investment grade at all three agencies and moved lower in the first half of 2026, which has reduced commercial paper access (Documentary Fact). Equity-method and other non-core assets are volatile: a USD 124 million impairment of the Whirlpool India stake was booked in Q3 2026 (Documentary Fact). Coverage of interest by ongoing EBITDA fell to 2.21x on an expense basis, and the proxy fixed charge ratio is 0.97x (Analyst Interpretation).

Issuer: WHIRLPOOL CORP /DE/ (issuer id whr; registrant name in the filings: WHIRLPOOL CORPORATION, Delaware, commission file number 1-3932; NYSE ticker WHR). As-of date and evidence cutoff: 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit snapshot, minimum module set (source readiness, then financial base, business and transaction, credit view and evidence trace). Reporting currency USD, in millions of dollars as the filings print it. Current period Q3 2026 (quarter ended 2026-09-30), prior period FY2025 (year ended 2025-12-31).

The question for this module is whether the pinned source set can support the four downstream modules and what remains blocked. It is a source-sufficiency review: no credit conclusion, no legal interpretation and no normalised figure is given here.
## Sources

The seven issuer sources below are the pinned text conversions of the filed documents (one row of text per source page). The sha256 values are those of the pinned `.jsonl` files, not the sha256 of the original HTML that each file prints on its first page. The context file is run settings, not issuer evidence.

Its deal terms, quotes, ratings, valuation, assumptions and research questions are blank or empty; blanks are not treated as zero.
Upstream handoffs: none. This is the first module of the run and CP-OS supplied no handoff.
Locators below use `file page:N`, where N is the pinned source chunk shown as page N, not the printed page number.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven filings and releases are enough to run the financial base, business and transaction, credit view and evidence trace modules, each with stated limitations. None is blocked and none needs a missing source before it can start. | Medium | No financing documents, no investor presentation and no third-party ratings reports are supplied, so debt terms and covenants rest on the issuer's own filing summaries. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Annual and all three quarterly filings of the one registrant are present, with matching earnings releases for each quarter. | Period coverage is complete for a latest-quarter and prior-year view. | High |

| Debt is itemised by instrument only in the annual report, before the June 2026 refinancing. | Current debt composition and maturities must be rebuilt from narrative notes and balance sheet lines. | Medium |

| The new asset-based facility and second lien notes are described only in filing text; the agreements are not supplied. | Covenant levels and borrowing capacity cannot be tested against executed terms. | Medium |
| Whirlpool India was deconsolidated in late 2025, so some prior-year comparatives include a business no longer consolidated. | Year-on-year trends need a like-for-like caution. | Medium |
| Interim cash paid for interest and taxes is not printed in the quarterly filings. | Cash interest cover for the latest period cannot be taken directly from the sources. | Medium |
### Readiness view

The pinned source set can support all four requested modules, each as READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, and none is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED. Authority is good: the filed 10-K and three filed 10-Qs control the financial and note facts, and the three earnings releases supply attributed management narrative, non-GAAP reconciliations and guidance. The strongest contrary evidence is what is absent rather than what conflicts: no executed financing documents, no investor presentation, no rating-agency reports and no interim cash interest or tax figures. Those absences narrow what the downstream modules can say about covenants, instrument terms and cash interest cover, and they should be carried forward as stated limitations. The next evidence action is to run the financial base module on the filed statements, then the business and transaction module, with these gaps passed on explicitly. This is source sufficiency only; it does not say that any downstream analysis has been done.
### Source register
| Source | Document family and authority | Entity and perimeter | Period and basis | Key locators read |

| 10-K, FY2025 | Filed annual report; audited; controls the annual financial and note facts. Audit opinion by Ernst & Young LLP dated February 11, 2026 (10-K page:155, "Chicago, Illinois February 11, 2026"). | Whirlpool Corporation and consolidated subsidiaries. Whirlpool India deconsolidated; prior segment information recast (10-K page:4). | Year ended 2025-12-31, with 2024 and 2023 comparatives; USD millions. | Statements: 10-K pages:75-77. Debt note: 10-K pages:100-101. Segment note: 10-K pages:131-133. Liquidity: 10-K page:57. |

| 10-Q, Q1 2026 | Filed interim report; unaudited; signed May 7, 2026 (10-Q Q1 page:58). | Same registrant, same consolidation basis. | Three months ended 2026-03-31, with prior-year and 2025-12-31 balance sheet comparatives. | Statements: 10-Q Q1 pages:5-6. Financing: page:15. Segments: page:36. Liquidity: page:43. |

| 10-Q, Q2 2026 | Filed interim report; unaudited; signed August 4, 2026 (10-Q Q2 page:64). | Same. | Three and six months ended 2026-06-30. | Statements: 10-Q Q2 pages:5-6. Financing: pages:17-20. Segments: page:40. Liquidity: page:48. |

| 10-Q, Q3 2026 | Filed interim report; unaudited; signed October 27, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:68). The latest filed financial statements before the cutoff. | Same. | Three and nine months ended 2026-09-30, with the 2025-12-31 balance sheet comparative. | Statements: 10-Q Q3 pages:5-7. Notes 1, 5, 6: pages:8-27. Segments: pages:43-44. Liquidity and outlook: pages:52-59. Risk factors: page:67. |

| EX-99.1, May 6, 2026 | Earnings release; management narrative, reported and non-GAAP figures, outlook; below the filing in authority. | Same registrant. | Q1 2026. | Release dated "BENTON HARBOR, Mich., May 6, 2026"; balance sheet page:7; measure definitions pages:8-9. |
| EX-99.1, August 3, 2026 | Earnings release; same standing. | Same. | Q2 2026. | Dated "August 3, 2026"; balance sheet page:7; definitions pages:8-9. |

| EX-99.1, October 26, 2026 | Earnings release; same standing. | Same. Footnote on page:1: "*Includes results from our previously-owned India business" for the 2025 comparative. | Q3 2026 and nine months; EBIT reconciliations for Q4 2025 through Q3 2026 and FY2025 and FY2024 (pages:11-18); full-year 2026 outlook (page:2). | Results page:1; outlook page:2; statements pages:5-8; reconciliations pages:11-20; footnotes pages:21-24; organic sales page:26. |

Version relationships. The three 10-Qs are separate periodic reports for successive periods, not versions of each other; none supersedes the 10-K. Each release is a separate source for its quarter and is retained beside the filing for the same quarter. The 10-K and the 10-Qs share one registrant, so there is no parent, subsidiary or combined-filing split to resolve. Within the debt, the 10-Q Q3 names the roles it prints: the Company as issuer of the Secured Notes; guarantors are "each domestic and Canadian subsidiary of the Company that is a borrower under, or a guarantor of" the ABL Credit Facility (10-Q Q3 page:18); euro notes were issued by the Company's "wholly owned subsidiary" (10-Q Q3 page:18), named on page:28 as Whirlpool Finance Luxembourg S.a.r.l.; the 10-K states that "For outstanding notes issued by our wholly-owned subsidiaries the debt is fully and unconditionally guaranteed by the Company" (10-K page:101). No restricted or unrestricted subsidiary distinction is printed.
### Consumer readiness
| Consumer | Status | Evidence in the sources | Limitations carried forward |

| Financial base (CP-1) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Annual statements for FY2025 (10-K pages:75-77); quarterly and year-to-date statements for Q1, six months and nine months of 2026 (10-Q pages as in the register); segment tables with net sales, EBIT, depreciation and amortization and capital expenditure (10-Q Q3 pages:43-44); quarterly EBIT reconciliations (release Q3 pages:11-18). | Interim cash paid for interest and taxes not printed (gap G1); instrument-level debt only at 2025-12-31 (G2); prior-year comparatives include India (G5); the Q4 2025 quarter is not a filed three-month statement and appears only in the release reconciliation (G6). |

| Business and transaction (CP-1A) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Business and segment description (10-K pages:4-17); 2026 transactions described in the notes and liquidity text: the February 2026 common and mandatory convertible preferred issuance, the June 16, 2026 second lien notes and asset-based facility, the Beko Europe stake sale and Russia agreement termination, sale-leasebacks and the purchase of previously leased assets (10-Q Q3 pages:11-13, 17-22, 53-57). | Executed transaction documents not supplied (G3); no investor presentation (G4); no management bridge. |

| Credit view (CP-2) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Balance sheet debt lines and liquidity text (10-Q Q3 pages:6, 52-58); the springing fixed charge coverage covenant described in words (10-Q Q3 pages:20-21); rating actions described in words (10-Q Q3 page:53); off-balance-sheet and guarantee amounts (10-Q Q3 pages:28, 58); factoring and supply chain finance (10-Q Q3 pages:12, 23). | Covenant definitions and borrowing base availability not supplied (G3, G7); rating-agency reports not supplied (G8); no market data, quotes or valuation inputs in the context (G9). |

| Evidence trace (CP-5) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Every figure can be located to a page chunk with the printed table or sentence. | Text extraction flattens tables; extraction success is not a fidelity review (G10). CP-5 also depends on the other modules' handoffs, which do not yet exist; that is sequencing, not a source condition. |

For the report sections the run will build (key findings, company operating model, chart strip, financial credit metrics, strengths and weaknesses, company profile, transaction summary), the chart strip needs leverage, interest cover, liquidity and debt maturities. Leverage inputs (debt lines, cash, EBIT and D and A) and liquidity inputs (cash, committed facilities, amounts drawn) are in the sources. The maturity table is printed only at 2025-12-31 and predates the refinancing (G2). Interest cover can use interest expense, which is printed for each period, but not cash interest for interim periods (G1).
### Strongest contrary evidence and what the sources do not settle

- Perimeter. The 10-K says that "the operations previously reported within the MDA Asia segment are no longer reported as a segment as a result of the deconsolidation of Whirlpool India" (10-K page:4), and the Q3 release flags the 2025 comparative as including the India business (release Q3 page:1). A trend analysis that does not adjust for this would overstate the decline; the release itself shows a like-for-like organic sales measure that removes India sales (release Q3 page:26). The sources do not print a full like-for-like FY2025 income statement.

- Definition difference. Segment-note total EBIT for Q3 2026 is "$ (128)" (10-Q Q3 page:43) and ties to the release's reported EBIT of "$ (128)"; the release's ongoing EBIT of "$ 97" (release Q3 page:11) excludes restructuring, an equity method impairment, M&A costs and a trade customer bankruptcy charge. The two are different measures, both issuer-defined, and downstream modules must label which they use.

- Management claim versus filing. The release says the company has "preserved a clear debt maturity ladder until 2028" (release Q3 page:1). The 10-Q Q3 supports part of this: "We have $14 million of debt maturing in the next twelve months" (10-Q Q3 page:53). The 10-Q does not itself print a maturity table after the refinancing, so the 2028 claim is an attributed management statement that a downstream module cannot verify from a table.

- Net leverage. The releases define "Net debt leverage" and "Ongoing EBITDA" (release Q3 page:9) but the pinned text does not print a computed ratio. The release outlook gives "Net debt below $4.5 billion at year end" (release Q3 page:2), a forward management statement, not a reported ratio.
## Calculations

None. This module does not calculate, normalise or reconcile figures. Counts used above: seven issuer sources with 157, 58, 64, 68, 18, 20 and 26 pages; every page is retained in the pinned conversion and none was excluded. The only comparisons made are label matches between printed figures (Q3 2026 EBIT of "$ (128)" appears on both 10-Q Q3 page:43 and release Q3 page:11).
## Gaps
| Ref | Gap | Severity | Affected consumers | Remediation |

| G1 | Cash paid for interest and for income taxes is printed only for full years in the 10-K ("Cash paid for interest $ 350 $ 352 $ 370" for 2025, 2024 and 2023, 10-K page:77). Searches of the three 10-Qs and three releases for "cash paid", "interest paid" and "supplemental disclosure" found nothing for interim periods. | Medium | Financial base, credit view | Use full-year cash interest only for FY2025; use interest expense for interim periods and label it as expense, not cash. |

| G2 | The instrument-level debt table with rates, amounts and maturities is printed only at 2025-12-31 (10-K pages:100-101), before the June 2026 refinancing. The 10-Qs describe the new notes in text (a USD 1.0 billion 7.500% issue due 2031 and a USD 1.0 billion 7.875% issue due 2034, 10-Q Q3 page:17) and the repayment of the 1.250% 2026 and 1.100% 2027 euro notes and the unsecured revolver (page:18), but carry no table by instrument at 2026-09-30. | Medium | Financial base, credit view, chart strip | Rebuild the current stack from the 10-K table, the Note 5 text and the balance sheet lines, and label what is rebuilt. |

| G3 | Executed financing documents are not supplied: the June 2026 indenture, the ABL Credit and Guaranty Agreement and the 2030 and 2033 note terms. The context states legal documents "none". Covenants are known only from the issuer's summaries (10-Q Q3 pages:18, 20-21). | Medium | Credit view, business and transaction | Treat covenant and security terms as issuer-summarised; do not infer definitions. |

| G4 | No investor presentation or earnings deck is supplied; the three releases stand in. Releases are text only here, and no chart or image content is claimed. | Low | Business and transaction | Use the releases as attributed management claims. |

| G5 | Prior-year comparatives include Whirlpool India until its deconsolidation on December 1, 2025 (10-Q Q3 page:14); only a Q3 sales removal is printed (release Q3 page:26). | Medium | Financial base, credit view | Compare like-for-like only where the release provides it; otherwise label the perimeter change. |

| G6 | Q4 2025 and fourth-quarter trailing figures are not a filed three-month statement; the release gives a Q4 2025 EBIT reconciliation (release Q3 page:14). Trailing twelve months would be built from FY2025 and nine-month figures. | Low | Financial base | Build trailing figures in the financial base module with inputs shown. |

| G7 | The ABL borrowing base, Availability and Line Cap amounts, and any letters of credit drawn on the ABL, are not printed. Searches for "availability", "Line Cap", "borrowing base" and "letters of credit" found only the covenant trigger text and unrelated letters of credit (synthetic leases, 10-Q Q3 page:10; off-balance-sheet, page:58). The 10-Q says "$0 million outstanding under the ABL Credit Facility" (10-Q Q3 page:54). | Medium | Credit view | Report committed amounts and amounts drawn as printed; state that usable availability is not supplied. |
| G8 | No rating-agency reports; ratings appear only as narrative (10-Q Q3 page:53). The context ratings list is empty. | Low | Credit view | Cite the narrative as issuer-reported. |
| G9 | Context market data, quotes, valuation inputs, deal terms and research questions are blank. | Low | Credit view | Not needed for the selected modules; do not treat blanks as zero. |

| G10 | Text extraction only. Tables are flattened, XBRL tags are not available, and no fidelity review of the conversion has been done. Figures are as printed in the conversion. | Low | All | Open each locator before relying on it. |

| G11 | The 10-K and 10-Qs carry no guarantor financial information in the pinned text beyond narrative; the 10-K exhibit list refers to a "List of Guarantors and Subsidiary Issuers of Guaranteed Securities" incorporated by reference (10-K page:149) that is not supplied. | Low | Credit view | Name guarantor roles only as the Note 5 text prints them. |

No source in the set is blocked, draft, unsigned or stale at the cutoff: the latest filing is signed October 27, 2026 and the latest release is dated October 26, 2026, both before 2026-11-05. No conflict between sources was found in the figures compared (balance sheet debt lines are identical in the 10-Q Q3 and release Q3, for example "Long-term debt 6,838 5,583" on 10-Q Q3 page:6 and release Q3 page:7). Every fact used is dated on or before the cutoff.
## Next module

Run the financial base module next, on the filed statements and notes, passing it gaps G1, G2, G5 and G6 and the definition difference between reported EBIT and ongoing EBIT. Then run the business and transaction module with G3 and G4. The credit view should receive G2, G3, G7 and G8, and the evidence trace should open locators in the filed statements before any release figure.

Issuer: WHIRLPOOL CORP /DE/ (issuer id whr; registrant WHIRLPOOL CORPORATION, ticker WHR). As-of date and evidence cutoff: 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit snapshot. Scope of this module: the financial base for the credit view, being reported statements, the definition review, leverage, interest cover, liquidity, debt maturities and cash flow, for FY2024, FY2025, nine months 2025, nine months 2026 and the twelve months to September 30, 2026 (LTM Q3 2026). Reporting currency USD, in millions as the filings print it; no other currency is used for any statement figure (euro-denominated notes are carried in USD in the filings). Perimeter: Whirlpool Corporation and consolidated subsidiaries; there is no subsidiary issuer or combined filing to separate.
## Sources
Issuer sources relied on (pinned text conversions; sha256 of the pinned files):
| Source (exact name) | sha256 |
| EX-99.1_2026-05-06_exhibit991pressrelease0331.htm.jsonl | 95b2ef1bae0716bbeb58c9c34ddb215005331537ecf7f29431fb7a2c2c9fd7ca |
| EX-99.1_2026-08-03_exhibit991pressrelease0630.htm.jsonl | b491ad294927787c02725c1a866e27f9e64402f8ea8aae9c4fd1904e04af4f8b |
| EX-99.1_2026-10-26_exhibit991pressrelease0930.htm.jsonl | c58aa3164f5692dfdb8e88300126ff35ac0e51e9ac5dd75d63c08d88b2ba7c69 |

Supplied handoff: CP-0 (source readiness), sha256 57c8443c6c648363633bdf1bf18dc588ac6f20998e98976e8abae94edbb6ab9f. This module opened it and carries forward its gaps G1 (interim cash interest and taxes not printed), G2 (instrument-level debt only at 2025-12-31), G5 (India in prior-year comparatives), G6 (Q4 2025 is not a filed three-month statement) and G7 (ABL availability not printed). Locators use `file page:N`, the pinned source chunk, not the printed page. Abbreviations: 10-K = FY2025 annual report; 10-Q Q1, Q2, Q3 = the 2026 quarterly reports; Release Q1, Q2, Q3 = the earnings releases of May 6, August 3 and October 26, 2026.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Leverage on company ongoing earnings plus depreciation rose to 9.52x total debt for the twelve months to Q3 2026 from 6.11x in FY2025, with debt of 6,852 million. The June refinancing cleared 2026 and 2027 maturities. | Medium | Interim cash interest is not printed, and EBITDA is built by the analyst from company ongoing EBIT plus cash flow depreciation, so ratios depend on that definition. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Ongoing EBITDA for the latest twelve months is 720 million against 1,067 million in FY2025, while total debt moved little. | Leverage and interest cover weakened because earnings fell, not because debt rose. | Medium |

| The June 2026 refinancing replaced unsecured bank debt and the 2026 and 2027 euro notes with second lien notes and a secured asset-based facility. | Near-term maturities are cleared, but existing unsecured creditors now rank behind secured debt. | Medium |

| Nine-month cash from operations was negative 826 million, and year-end net debt guidance relies on a large fourth-quarter inflow. | Deleveraging depends on working capital release rather than earnings. | Medium |

| Cash was 1,103 million and undrawn committed facilities were 2,193 million at September 30, 2026. | Headline liquidity looks adequate, but usable asset-based availability depends on a borrowing base that is not disclosed. | Medium |
| Cash paid for interest is printed only for full years. | Cash interest cover for the latest period cannot be read directly from the sources. | High |
### Financial base view

Whirlpool entered the latest quarter with weaker earnings and a much longer, more secured debt stack than a year earlier. On the company's own ongoing EBIT plus cash flow depreciation and amortization, EBITDA for the twelve months to September 30, 2026 is 720 million, down from 1,067 million in FY2025 and 1,220 million in FY2024. Total debt (notes payable, current maturities and long-term debt) was 6,852 million at September 30, 2026 against 6,520 million at December 31, 2025, so total debt over ongoing EBITDA is 9.52x against 6.11x, and net debt over ongoing EBITDA is 7.98x against 5.48x. Using the reported operating profit basis instead, the same ratios are 8.46x and 7.10x for the latest twelve months, and the direction is the same. Reported earnings were also hit in the third quarter by a 124 million impairment of the Whirlpool India equity stake and a 54 million trade customer bankruptcy charge, and flattered in earlier periods by disposal gains. ### Source context

All seven issuer sources describe one registrant on one consolidated perimeter, in USD millions, on a US GAAP basis (10-Q Q3 page:8). The 10-K is audited (Ernst & Young LLP opinion dated February 11, 2026, 10-K page:155); the 10-Qs are unaudited. FY2024 and FY2025 statements come from the 10-K; the 2026 interim statements from the three 10-Qs; ongoing (non-GAAP) EBIT by quarter from the Release Q3 reconciliations, which are management measures and sit below the filings in authority. Comparatives were reclassified by the issuer: for example "Prepaid and other current assets" of 654 at 2025-12-31 in the 10-K (page:76) is shown in the 10-Q Q3 as 535 plus 119 of "Other receivables" (page:6). No restatement of a reported total was found in the comparisons made.
### Definition review

- Total debt is notes payable, current maturities of long-term debt and long-term debt, which is how the releases define net debt before deducting cash (Release Q3 page:9). It excludes lease liabilities (noncurrent 863 at 2026-09-30, 10-Q Q3 page:6), pensions and retiree medical (83 and 91 on the same page), the 575 mandatory convertible preferred, supply chain finance of 650 recorded in accounts payable (10-Q Q3 page:12) and 157 of transferred receivables still serviced by the Company (10-Q Q3 page:23).

- EBITDA is not a printed figure. The releases define ongoing EBITDA and net debt leverage but print no value (Release Q3 page:9), and searches of all sources found no printed ratio. This module builds ongoing EBITDA as company ongoing EBIT plus cash flow D&A. The D&A may include accelerated depreciation that the ongoing measure already adds back inside restructuring (the Supsa plan includes accelerated depreciation, 10-Q Q3 page:41), so the figure could modestly overstate ongoing EBITDA. The amount is not printed.

- Total EBIT in the 10-K and 10-Q segment notes is the company definition: operating profit less interest and sundry (income) expense plus equity method results (10-K page:133; 10-Q Q3 page:44). It is not an operating measure and was (128) in Q3 2026 after the 124 India impairment.

- Ongoing EBIT excludes restructuring (35 in Q3 2026), the equity method impairment (124), M&A transaction items (13) and the trade customer bankruptcy charge (54) (Release Q3 page:11). It does not exclude the 2026 sale-leaseback gains booked in cost of products sold (about 21 in Q2 and 28 in Q3 per 10-Q Q3 pages:11-12) or the DIFAL and labor tax gains of about 35, 8 and 27 (10-Q Q3 pages:25-26); whether these sit inside ongoing EBIT is not stated.
- The covenant definitions that matter to lenders are not supplied (CP-0 gap G3). Management's ratios and the ABL fixed charge coverage test will not equal anything computed here.
### Narrative review by dimension

- Leverage. Total debt rose by 332 from December 31, 2025 to September 30, 2026 (6,520 to 6,852) while ongoing EBITDA fell, so the ratio worsened on both terms. Net debt of 5,749 compares with the company's year-end expectation of "Net debt below $4.5 billion at year end" (Release Q3 page:2); closing that distance in one quarter is about 1,249, a derived figure that rests entirely on management guidance.

- Coverage. Ongoing EBITDA over interest expense fell from 3.13x in FY2025 to 2.21x over the latest twelve months. The Q3 2026 interest expense of 102 is the highest quarter in the series shown and comes after the June issue of the 7.500% and 7.875% secured notes and the repayment of the euro notes and bank debt; the sources do not print the run-rate effect or attribute the increase. The 10-K facility required interest coverage of at least 3.0 (10-K page:104), and a May 2026 amendment excluded the March 31, 2026 quarter from that test (10-Q Q1 page:17). The new ABL has a springing fixed charge coverage ratio of not less than 1.00 to 1.00, tested only if Availability falls below the greater of 10% of the Line Cap and 135 (10-Q Q3 pages:20-21); the level and headroom cannot be computed from the sources.

- Cash flow quality. Cash used in operations was 826 for nine months 2026 against 669 used in nine months 2025, with accounts payable (306), accrued advertising and promotions (318) and other (168) among the larger movements (10-Q Q3 page:7). Management guides full-year cash from operations of about 700 and free cash flow of about 300 (Release Q3 page:2), which implies a fourth-quarter operating inflow of about 1,526 (700 less the nine-month outflow of 826 as a negative); this is derived from guidance, not reported.

- Liquidity. Cash of 1,103 and 2,193 of undrawn committed facilities total 3,296, down from 4,101 at December 31, 2025 (669 plus 3,432). The nominal undrawn amount overstates usable liquidity because the ABL is limited by a borrowing base and by the springing covenant, and because letters of credit that may use the ABL are not printed. The 14 of debt due within twelve months is small against cash.

- Data quality. Figures are from filed statements and notes except ongoing EBIT, which is a management reconciliation. The 9M 2025 free cash flow difference (908 computed against 907 printed) and quarterly rounding (Q1 to Q3 2026 EBIT sums to 35 against 34 printed for nine months) are rounding-sized.
- Definition risks. See Definition review. The most material are the EBITDA construction, the exclusion of leases, supply chain finance and the preferred from debt, and the India perimeter.
- Key gaps. See Gaps.

Off-balance-sheet and contingent claims noted for the credit view, none included in total debt: supply chain finance of 650 (772 at 2025-12-31), synthetic lease residual value guarantees of up to about 96 (504 at 2025-12-31) with letters of credit of 147, guarantees of indebtedness and lines of credit for subsidiaries of about 1.2 billion (3.3 billion at 2025-12-31), bank guarantees, letters of credit and surety bonds of about 578, and Brazil tax assessments of about 545 (BEFIEX), 88 (PIS/COFINS), 61 (IPI Amnesty) and 112 unreserved (DIFAL), where the BEFIEX and PIS/COFINS amounts are stated as not accrued, DIFAL is accrued in some states and unreserved in others, and the IPI Amnesty accrual is not stated (10-Q Q3 pages:10, 12, 24-25, 28, 58). These amounts are as printed and are not added together.

All figures are USD millions from the cited pages. LTM Q3 2026 means FY2025 less nine months 2025 plus nine months 2026.
3. Operating profit LTM: 838 - 595 + 185 = 428. Nine months 2025 and 2026 come from 10-Q Q3 page:5.
4. Total EBIT LTM: 824 - 590 + 34 = 268. The quarterly sum 234 + 9 + 154 - 128 = 269; the difference of 1 is rounding in the printed quarters.
9. Interest expense LTM: 341 - 256 + 241 = 326.

15. Cash flow: LTM cash from operations 470 + 669 - 826 = 313; LTM capital expenditures 389 - 239 + 255 = 405; LTM operating cash flow less capital expenditures 313 - 405 = (92). Nine months 2025: (669) - 239 = (908); nine months 2026: (826) - 255 = (1,081). Dividends LTM 300 - 248 + 81 = 133.
16. Net earnings available to Whirlpool LTM: 318 - 210 - 231 = (123).

18. Maturity chart: 2031 and later = 3,008 + 1,000 + 1,000 = 5,008. Cross-check to the balance sheet: 14 + 585 + 695 + 592 + 5,008 = 6,894 against total debt of 6,852, a difference of 42 that the sources do not explain (issue discount and costs on the new notes, euro remeasurement and other items are not printed). Debt bridge: 6,169 - 587 - 703 + 2,000 = 6,879 against 6,838 long-term debt including current maturities at 2026-09-30, a difference of 41, treated the same way.

19. Change in debt and guidance gap: 6,852 - 6,520 = 332 increase in total debt; 5,749 - 4,500 = 1,249 net debt reduction implied by the guidance of net debt below 4,500 (derived, ceiling not target); implied fourth-quarter operating inflow 700 - (-826) = 1,526.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Whirlpool is a listed, widely held appliance maker with no sponsor in the sources. Its 2026 actions were equity issuance, a dividend cut and a secured refinancing, which helped liquidity but placed unsecured creditors behind secured debt. | Medium | The indentures, the asset-based credit agreement and the shareholder register are not supplied, so creditor control rights and ownership above five percent cannot be assessed. |

| North America generates most sales, and Lowe's alone was about 15% of 2025 net sales and about 44% of receivables at year end. | Customer concentration ties cash conversion and credit risk to one retailer, with no long-term sales contracts. | High |

| In February 2026 Whirlpool raised 524 million of common equity and 557 million of mandatory convertible preferred, and later suspended the common dividend. | Equity support and cash retention are supportive, but the preferred dividend is cumulative and ranks ahead of common. | High |

| The June 2026 refinancing put a first-lien asset-based facility and 2,000 million of second lien notes on one collateral pool. | Secured lenders now rank ahead of the unsecured notes, whose lien covenants were not reviewed because the indentures are not supplied. | Medium |

| Management cut the full-year 2026 earnings outlook twice after the first quarter, and a Latin American customer bankruptcy added a 54 million charge. | Earnings visibility is low; recovery depends on price increases holding against weak North American demand. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

Whirlpool is a listed, widely held major and small appliance manufacturer with no sponsor named in the sources, and its recent transactions have been defensive: sell down non-core stakes, raise equity, cut distributions, and refinance bank and euro debt into secured paper. The business is concentrated in North America, which supplied most nine-month 2026 net sales of 10,467 million through MDA North America at 7,141 million, and in one retail channel, with Lowe's about 15% of 2025 net sales. Demand in North America is soft, tariffs and cost inflation are compressing margins, and management has cut its 2026 earnings outlook twice since May. The June 2026 refinancing gave the company a 2,000 million asset-based facility, undrawn at quarter end, and replaced the 2026 and 2027 euro notes with second lien notes, so near-term maturities are cleared at the cost of subordinating unsecured creditors in the collateral pool. Governance behaviour in the sources is on balance supportive of liquidity (equity issuance, dividend cuts, asset sales and sale-leasebacks) with a mixed effect on creditor ranking. The decisive unknowns are legal: what the indentures permit, what the ABL borrowing base allows, and who the large holders are, none of which is supplied. Source evidence is primary and dated, except management characterisations, which are labelled.

| Segments | Three segments: MDA North America, MDA Latin America, SDA Global. The transactions that matter to creditors are these, all dated on or before the cutoff of 2026-11-05. On February 27, 2026 Whirlpool issued 11,500,000 depositary shares of its 8.50% Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock (net cash proceeds 557 million) and 7,898,550 common shares at 69 dollars per share (net cash proceeds 524 million), and used about 900 million of the proceeds to repay part of its prior revolving credit facility (10-Q Q3 pages:52-53, 57). In March 2026 it paid 157 million to buy the legal title to five assets previously held under synthetic leases (10-Q Q3 page:11). In May 2026 it amended the Long-Term Credit Agreement to cut the commitment from 3.50 billion to 2.25 billion, excluded the March 31, 2026 quarter from the interest coverage test and required a full refinancing before July 1, 2026 (10-Q Q1 page:17). In June 2026 it agreed with Arcelik to sell its remaining 25% of Beko Europe, terminate deferred rights from the 2022 Russian business divestiture and release accrued indemnities, for net cash of 84 million plus a 2.9% Arcelik stake, booking a gain of 139 million (10-Q Q3 pages:13, 46). On June 16, 2026 it issued 1,000 million of 7.500% Senior Secured Second Lien Notes due 2031 and 1,000 million of 7.875% Senior Secured Second Lien Notes due 2034 under a Rule 144A private placement, entered a new asset-based credit facility of up to 2,000 million with J.P. Morgan as agent, and terminated the Long-Term Credit Agreement; the notes and the facility share one collateral pool, first-priority for the facility and second-priority for the notes, guaranteed by domestic and Canadian subsidiaries that are ABL obligors. The proceeds and ABL borrowings repaid the 1.250% Senior Notes due 2026, the 1.100% Senior Notes due 2027 and the unsecured revolver by July 1, 2026, with 212 million of cash restricted at June 30 for that payment (10-Q Q3 pages:17-21; 10-Q Q2 page:7). The December 2025 background is the sale of about 11% of Whirlpool India for about 166 million, reducing ownership from 51% to about 40%, with deconsolidation and a gain of 251 million (10-Q Q3 page:45). Debt raised in 2026 and its effect on the debt stack and liquidity are quantified in CP-1: total debt of 6,852 million, cash of 1,103 million and undrawn committed facilities of 2,193 million at September 30, 2026. No transaction was reported after September 30, 2026 other than management statements in the October 26, 2026 release (Q4 price increases and the net debt expectation); the 10-Q Q3 reports "ITEM 5. OTHER INFORMATION None." (10-Q Q3 page:68). The executed indenture and ABL agreement are not supplied, so lien, guarantee, baskets and permitted payment terms are known only as the issuer summarises them.

This is the fundamental credit view of WHIRLPOOL CORP /DE/ (whr) as of 2026-11-05, in the credit snapshot pathway, built on the financial base and the business and transaction handoffs. It covers business risk, financial risk, liquidity, covenants, claims outside reported debt and the gaps that limit them, in USD millions as the filings print them. It gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Whirlpool's credit is weak and weakening but not in near-term distress: liquidity and a maturity runway to 2028 offset leverage of 9.52x total debt on ongoing EBITDA and negative nine-month operating cash flow. | Medium | Covenant definitions, borrowing base availability and interim cash interest are not supplied, so headroom and usable liquidity cannot be measured. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Total debt of USD 6,852 million is 9.52x ongoing EBITDA of USD 720 million for the latest twelve months, against 6.11x in FY2025. | Leverage is high for a non-investment-grade issuer and rose because earnings fell, not because debt grew much. | Medium |

| After the June 2026 refinancing only USD 14 million falls due in the next twelve months and USD 585 million in 2028. | Refinancing risk is deferred rather than removed; most debt falls due from 2031 onward. | Medium |

| Secured debt now includes an undrawn USD 2,000 million asset-based facility and USD 2,000 million of second lien notes on one collateral pool. | Unsecured noteholders rank behind secured lenders on that collateral. | Medium |

| An indicative fixed charge proxy is 0.97x against the 1.00x springing covenant, which applies only if ABL availability is low. | There is little cushion if earnings or the borrowing base weaken further. | Low |

| Guidance implies a fourth-quarter operating cash inflow of about USD 1,526 million to reach year-end net debt below USD 4.5 billion. | Deleveraging depends on a working capital release rather than earnings. | Low |
### Credit view

Whirlpool is a stretched, non-investment-grade credit with a funded runway to 2028 but little earnings cushion. The strongest support is liquidity and structure: USD 1,103 million of cash and USD 2,193 million of undrawn committed facilities at September 30, 2026, equity raised in February, and only USD 14 million due within twelve months after the June refinancing. The weakest point is earnings: ongoing EBITDA for the latest twelve months is USD 720 million against total debt of USD 6,852 million, or 9.52x, with operating cash flow of negative USD 826 million for nine months and interest expense now running near USD 100 million a quarter. What decides the outcome is whether price increases and cost take-out restore North American margins, and whether year-end working capital release materialises, before the secured facility's borrowing base and its fixed charge test begin to bind.
### Key findings

Leverage has moved sharply the wrong way. Total debt over ongoing EBITDA was 5.43x in FY2024, 6.11x in FY2025 and is 9.52x for the twelve months to September 30, 2026, with net debt over ongoing EBITDA of 7.98x. On the stricter operating-profit basis the latest ratios are 8.46x and 7.10x, so the conclusion does not depend on which EBITDA is used. Total debt rose by USD 332 million over the first nine months of 2026 while ongoing EBITDA fell from USD 1,067 million in FY2025 to USD 720 million for the latest twelve months. The issuer does not print a leverage ratio, so every ratio here is analyst-built.

The refinancing bought time and cost carry. The June 2026 issue of USD 1,000 million of 7.500% notes due 2031 and USD 1,000 million of 7.875% notes due 2034 carries about USD 154 million of annual coupon (derived from the stated rates), replacing euro notes with coupons of 1.25% and 1.10% on about USD 1,290 million of carrying value, so roughly USD 139 million of added annual coupon before any saving on the repaid revolver. Quarterly interest expense reached USD 102 million in Q3 2026 against USD 63 million in Q2, and management guides full-year 2026 interest of about USD 350 million and Q4 interest of about USD 103 million. Ongoing EBITDA over annualised Q3 interest of USD 408 million is 1.76x, and guided full-year 2026 ongoing EBIT of about USD 293 million is 0.84x guided interest. Cash interest is not printed for the interim periods, so these are expense-based.

Liquidity is adequate on paper and uncertain in substance. Cash of USD 1,103 million and undrawn commitments of USD 2,193 million total USD 3,296 million, down from USD 4,101 million at December 31, 2025, and the nominal undrawn amount is mostly an ABL (USD 2,000 million) limited by a borrowing base the filings do not disclose. Operating cash flow was negative USD 826 million for nine months and management's guidance of about USD 700 million for the year implies a fourth-quarter inflow of about USD 1,526 million. That is a seasonal working capital release, not a trend, and it carries execution risk.

Covenant headroom is thin on every proxy available. The ABL tests fixed charge coverage of 1.00x only when Availability falls below the greater of 10% of the Line Cap and USD 135 million. An indicative proxy of ongoing EBITDA less capital expenditures over interest expense is 0.97x, so if availability tightened the test could bind. The proxy is not the covenant definition. The prior facility's interest coverage test of at least 3.0x was relaxed in May 2026 by excluding the first quarter, and expense-based cover has since fallen to 2.21x.

Creditor ranking has shifted. The ABL is first lien and the Secured Notes are second lien on the same collateral pool, secured by substantially all assets of the Company and the guarantors, while about USD 4.8 billion of senior unsecured notes (derived as total debt less the Secured Notes and notes payable) remain. Whether the unsecured note indentures allowed the lien grant or required equal and ratable security is not stated and the documents are not supplied. This is an open legal question, not an adverse finding.

Claims outside reported debt are material in aggregate. Supply chain finance of USD 650 million sits in payables, operating lease liabilities of USD 863 million noncurrent, a USD 575 million cumulative mandatory convertible preferred, Brazilian tax assessments (BEFIEX about USD 545 million, PIS/COFINS about USD 88 million, IPI Amnesty about USD 61 million, and USD 112 million unreserved for DIFAL), and USD 578 million of bank guarantees, letters of credit and surety bonds. None is in total debt.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Whirlpool holds scaled, long-established appliance franchises with leading positions in the Americas and a brand portfolio including Whirlpool, KitchenAid and Maytag (Documentary Fact; Management Language for the market-position wording). It has demonstrated market access in 2026, raising USD 524 million of common equity and USD 557 million of mandatory convertible preferred in February (Documentary Fact), and it suspended the common dividend, which retains cash (Documentary Fact). After the June refinancing near-term maturities are cleared: USD 14 million falls due in the next twelve months and USD 585 million in 2028 (Documentary Fact for the 14; Analyst Interpretation for the schedule, which is rebuilt). The asset-based facility of USD 2,000 million and Brazilian facilities of USD 193 million were undrawn at September 30, 2026 (Documentary Fact). Management is executing structural cost take-out and price increases, announced at 7% in North America and up to 10% in Latin America (Management Language), and the SDA Global segment earned segment EBIT of USD 124 million on USD 710 million of nine-month sales (Documentary Fact).

Weaknesses. Leverage of 9.52x total debt over ongoing EBITDA is high and rising (Analyst Interpretation on a Documentary Fact base). Ongoing EBIT for Q3 2026 was USD 97 million against USD 180 million a year earlier and management has cut its 2026 earnings outlook twice since May (Documentary Fact; Management Language for the outlook). North American demand is soft and one retailer is about 15% of sales and about 44% of receivables (Documentary Fact). Operating cash flow is negative on a nine-month basis, and year-end net debt guidance relies on a fourth-quarter release (Analyst Interpretation). The new secured structure subordinates unsecured creditors in the collateral pool and limits flexibility through indenture covenants and a borrowing base (Documentary Fact; legal capacity Insufficient Information). Ratings are below investment grade at all three agencies and moved lower in the first half of 2026, which has reduced commercial paper access (Documentary Fact). Equity-method and other non-core assets are volatile: a USD 124 million impairment of the Whirlpool India stake was booked in Q3 2026 (Documentary Fact). Coverage of interest by ongoing EBITDA fell to 2.21x on an expense basis, and the proxy fixed charge ratio is 0.97x (Analyst Interpretation).
### Assessment and thesis

Assessment (Analyst Interpretation, confidence Medium): the fundamental credit view is weak and weakening, with default risk in the next twelve months contained by liquidity and cleared maturities but with refinancing and covenant risk building as the secured layer grows and earnings stay low. Thesis: Whirlpool can service its debt through 2027 on its liquidity, but its credit quality depends on restoring North American margins and on a year-end working capital release that its own guidance requires.

| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Earnings shortfall | Weak North American demand, tariffs and cost inflation reduce ongoing EBITDA faster than debt falls. | Leverage stays above 9x and interest cover stays near 2x unless price and cost actions land. | Critical |

| Year-end working capital release | The guided net debt reduction requires a fourth-quarter operating inflow of about USD 1,526 million. | A shortfall leaves net debt above guidance and draws on the ABL. | Material |

| ABL availability and covenant | Borrowing base shrinks with inventory and receivables; the 1.00x test springs when availability is low. | Liquidity can fall faster than the nominal USD 2,193 million suggests. | Material |

| Structural subordination | Secured lenders hold first and second liens over the collateral pool ahead of the unsecured notes. | Lower recovery mechanics for unsecured creditors in stress (mechanic only, no recovery conclusion). | Material |

| Customer and receivable concentration | Lowe's is about 44% of year-end receivables; a Latin American customer bankruptcy cost USD 54 million. | Single-counterparty events hit sales, receivables and factoring capacity together. | Material |
| Contingent claims | Brazilian tax assessments, guarantees and synthetic lease obligations sit outside debt. | Adverse outcomes would draw on liquidity. | Minor to Material |
| Rating pressure | Below investment grade at all three agencies with negative outlooks cited. | Higher borrowing cost, reduced commercial paper access. | Material |

All inputs are USD millions from the cited pages or the financial base handoff.
1. Leverage and cover are those in the financial base: total debt 6,852 over ongoing EBITDA 720 is 9.52x; net debt 5,749 over 720 is 7.98x; 8.46x and 7.10x on operating-profit EBITDA of 810.
2. Annual coupon on the Secured Notes: 1,000 x 7.500% = 75.00; 1,000 x 7.875% = 78.75; total 153.75, shown as about 154.

3. Coupon on repaid euro notes at carrying value: 587 x 1.25% = 7.34 and 703 x 1.10% = 7.73, about 15 in total; added annual coupon 153.75 - 15.07 = about 139 (approximate; face values in euro and the saving on the repaid revolver are not printed).
4. Run-rate interest: Q3 2026 interest expense 102 x 4 = 408; ongoing EBITDA 720 / 408 = 1.76x. Guided ongoing EBIT 293 / guided interest expense 350 = 0.84x (EBIT basis, management guidance).

5. Fixed charge proxy: (ongoing EBITDA 720 - capital expenditures 405) / interest expense 326 = 315 / 326 = 0.97x. Capital expenditures LTM 405 = 389 - 239 + 255 and interest expense LTM 326 = 341 - 256 + 241 (financial base). Not the covenant.
6. Implied Q4 operating inflow: guided operating cash flow 700 - nine-month outflow (-826) = 1,526. Implied net debt reduction: 5,749 - 4,500 = 1,249 (a ceiling).

8. Unsecured notes: carrying values at 2025-12-31 of the 0.50% 2028, 4.75% 2029, 6.125% 2030, 2.40% 2031, 4.75% 2032, 5.50% 2033, 6.50% 2033, 5.75% 2034, 5.15% 2043, 4.50% 2046 and 4.60% 2050 notes: 586 + 697 + 600 + 300 + 298 + 300 + 600 + 299 + 249 + 497 + 493 = 4,919, about 4,900. Cross-check: total debt 6,852 - Secured Notes 2,000 - notes payable 14 = 4,838, about 4.8 billion; the 81 difference is not explained in the sources (discounts, "Other, net" of (39) and euro remeasurement are candidates).
9. Back-loading: 5,008 / 6,894 = 72.6%, shown as about 73%.
10. US cash: 3.7% x total assets 16,963 = about 628.
11. Preferred dividend: 575 x 8.50% = 48.9, about 49 a year.
12. Derived maturities against the balance sheet: 14 + 585 + 695 + 592 + 5,008 = 6,894; 6,894 - 6,852 = 42.
## Gaps
| Ref | Gap | Why it matters and action |

| C1 | Covenant definitions, ABL borrowing base, Availability, Line Cap and letters of credit drawn on the ABL are not supplied. | Headroom and usable liquidity cannot be measured. Request the ABL agreement, the latest borrowing base certificate and the compliance certificate. |
| C2 | Cash paid for interest for 2026 interim periods is not printed. | Cash interest cover cannot be read; expense-based cover is used. |

| C3 | Indentures and the lien and guarantee terms of the pre-2026 unsecured notes are not supplied. | Legal capacity for the lien grant and structural ranking cannot be tested. Insufficient Information, not an adverse finding. |
| C4 | No post-refinancing instrument table; the maturity profile is derived (a USD 42 million unexplained difference to the balance sheet remains). | Maturity wall shown is approximate. |

| C5 | Prior-year comparatives include Whirlpool India until December 2025. | Year-on-year trends overstate the decline of the continuing business; the release gives only a 2025 like-for-like ongoing EBIT of about USD 688 million. |
| C6 | Ratings reports, market prices and valuation inputs are not supplied; the context ratings field is blank. | No market-implied or agency-based view is formed. |
| C7 | Inherited from the business and transaction module: no sponsor or large holder data, no investor presentation. | Ownership-driven behaviour cannot be assessed beyond documented actions. |
